;Business and economy
*[[Economy of Japan]]
**[[Sony]] agrees to a [[USD|$]]2.3 billion deal where they will buy a controlling interest in [[EMI Music Publishing]]. The deal will mean that Sony would indirectly own 90% of the music publisher and its two million songs. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-44206075 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Israel–Paraguay relations]], [[Status of Jerusalem]]
**[[Paraguay]] opens its embassy in [[Jerusalem]], making Paraguay the third country, after the [[United States]] and [[Guatemala]], to transfer its diplomatic mission in [[Israel]] from [[Tel Aviv]] to Jerusalem. [https://www.politico.com/story/2018/05/21/paraguay-embassy-jerusalem-600780 (AP via ''Politico'')] 
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**U.S. Secretary of State [[Mike Pompeo]] says the U.S. will impose "the strongest sanctions in history" on Iran if it does not meet various demands, including ending [[Iran and weapons of mass destruction|its nuclear program]] and leaving the [[Syrian Civil War]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-usa/u-s-toughens-stance-on-iran-lists-sweeping-demands-idUSKCN1IM1DE (Reuters)]
**Iranian President [[Hassan Rouhani]] rejects Pompeo's demands, and Iranian Foreign Minister [[Mohammed Javad Zarif]] accuses the U.S. of "repeating past mistakes." [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/05/iran-hits-nuclear-deal-demands-180521173257818.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**The Syrian government declares Damascus as "completely safe" from militant groups for the first time in seven years as it forces out ISIS from the area. ([https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/syria/syria-declares-damascus-isis-free-for-first-time-in-seven-years-1.6100278 ''Haaretz'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Catholic sexual abuse cases in Australia]]
**[[Philip Wilson (archbishop)|Philip Wilson]], the [[Catholic]] [[archbishop]] of [[Adelaide]], [[Australia]], is convicted of concealing sexual abuse of children from authorities. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-44205985 (BBC)]
*''[[Epic Systems Corp. v. Lewis]]''
**The [[U.S. Supreme Court]] votes 5–4 to allow companies to enforce contracts which bar employees from entering [[class action]] lawsuits. [http://www.concordmonitor.com/Supreme-Court-rules-that-companies-can-require-workers-to-accept-individual-arbitration-17672780 (''The Washington Post'' via ''Concord Monitor'')]
